ABSENCE: The plan does not specify what `make hooks` should do if `.git/hooks/commit-msg` (Gerrit's hook) is absent when `pre-commit install` runs — there is no guard, error, or ordered dependency stated.
findings.finding: The Gerrit hook chaining mechanism has a silent-failure ordering gap: pre-commit's migration mode only preserves an existing `commit-msg` as `.legacy` — if `make hooks`/`make install` runs BEFORE Gerrit's commit-msg hook is curl-installed (e.g., a developer clones and runs `make install` first, or `make worktree` provisions a fresh clone), pre-commit installs its commit-msg shim with nothing to chain, and all subsequent commits silently lack a Change-Id, breaking every Gerrit push. The plan names `make hooks` as the guard but does not specify what it does when the Gerrit hook slot is absent at install time, nor does it guard against this ordering in `make worktree` (which calls `make install`).
findings.location: Approach section — 'Critical risk handled: Gerrit's commit-msg hook'; AC: 'make hooks verifies both hook types AND that Change-Id stamping survives'
scenarios: Developer clones the repo and immediately runs `make install` before completing CONTRIBUTING.md §1b — commit-msg slot gets the pre-commit shim with no .legacy; every commit on that machine will silently lack a Change-Id.

`make worktree` provisions a new worktree by calling `make install`, which calls `make hooks` — if the common hooks dir does not yet have Gerrit's commit-msg hook, the slot is silently claimed by pre-commit alone.
findings.suggested_fix: In the `make hooks` target, add a pre-install check: if `.git/hooks/commit-msg` does not exist (or does not contain Gerrit's hook), print an explicit error — 'Gerrit commit-msg hook not installed; run the curl install from CONTRIBUTING.md §1b first' — and exit non-zero before running `pre-commit install`. This prevents silent slot capture and makes the ordering explicit and enforced.

findings.finding: The plan's central install mechanism — 'a bare `pre-commit install` (what `make hooks` runs) installs BOTH hook types' via `default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, commit-msg]` — is asserted but not verified against the actual installed pre-commit binary's behavior. The `default_install_hook_types` config key is real (added in pre-commit 2.18), but its exact semantics when `pre-commit install` is called without an explicit `-t` flag have changed across versions and warrant a flag-level check. In some pre-commit versions, `default_install_hook_types` governs only the default when the key is absent (i.e., it sets what types are installed when none are specified at CLI or config level), but `pre-commit install` without `-t` may still only install `pre-commit` type unless the config key is properly honored. The plan's floor of `>=3.5` would cover this if behavior is as claimed, but this has not been directly observed via `pre-commit install --help` in this environment.

This guarantees both are installed regardless of how `default_install_hook_types` is interpreted, and is unambiguous.

findings.finding: The RETIRE path for `.git/hooks/commit-msg.legacy` is undefined. If a developer runs `pre-commit uninstall` (e.g., to switch tooling), pre-commit removes `.git/hooks/commit-msg` but leaves `commit-msg.legacy` as an orphan — nothing will ever invoke it again. Subsequent `git commit` calls succeed without stamping a `Change-Id`, silently breaking every Gerrit push. The plan's `make hooks` guard only checks the forward install path, not the teardown path.
findings.location: Approach section — 'make hooks now verifies BOTH hooks landed AND that Gerrit's Change-Id stamping survived'; AC line: 'make hooks verifies both hook types landed AND that Change-Id stamping survives'
scenarios: A developer decides to stop using pre-commit (or switches to a different hook manager) and runs `pre-commit uninstall`. `.git/hooks/commit-msg` is removed; `.git/hooks/commit-msg.legacy` remains but is never called. All subsequent commits silently lack a `Change-Id`, and every `git push` to Gerrit is rejected at the server with a missing Change-Id error — with no local warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `make unhooks` (or `hooks-uninstall`) target that: (1) runs `pre-commit uninstall`, (2) moves `.git/hooks/commit-msg.legacy` back to `.git/hooks/commit-msg` if the legacy file exists. Document this in CONTRIBUTING.md alongside the install instructions.
